name: Bahá’i Holy Places in Haifa and the Western Galilee
description: Seven sites across Haifa and the Western Galilee make up the holiest places of the Bahá'í faith, drawing pilgrims from around the world. The best known is the Shrine of the Báb, set on Mount Carmel's slope and surrounded by garden terraces. The other is the Shrine of Bahá'u'lláh near Acre, where the faith's founder was imprisoned under Ottoman rule. In 2008 they became the first sites tied to a relatively new religion to be inscribed.
